title: Nets look to overcome losing woes vs. Nic Claxton, Bulls on ABA Night
text:
Nets look to overcome losing woes vs. Nic Claxton, Bulls on ABA Night Rumors Stats Odds Betting Newsletter Shop NETS Nets look to overcome losing woes vs. Nic Claxton, Bulls on ABA Night
 Sharif Phillips-Keaton Nets Wire Nov. 18, 2026, 7:06 p.m. ET NEW YORK -- The Brooklyn Nets (3-10) have not yet "shocked the world" like they set out to do when training camp began in September following an exciting offseason of moves. Brooklyn has not been able to be on the same page as a young team that has several new players in the rotation, but the Nets are hoping to draw some inspiration from players in previous generations.
 "I think that winning can be absorbed by the kids. I think that would be the best thing, and a lot of that comes with the work, but also building that connected team," Fernandez said to the media prior to Wednesday's matchup against the Chicago Bulls . Not only will former Nets center Nic Claxton be making his return to Barclays Center for the first time since he was traded this offseason, but "ABA Night" should give the players some extra juice as well.
 "I see it the other way. It's 'this is what we did to get back into the game,' right? Instead of bringing too many negatives into [it], it's this is the type of team we want to be with cleaner coverages, but also being the aggressor," Fernandez explained when asked how the team can prevent falling behind by double digits. "At this moment, I want to focus on the positives and how to clean up and teach some of the things that we didn't do as well in the first half."
 The Nets enter Wednesday's matchup against the Bulls on a two-game losing streak and in their losses to the Memphis Grizzlies and Philadelphia 76ers, Brooklyn trailed by as many as 26 points and 24 points, respectively. Conversely, in the Nets' three wins this season, they have only trailed by 10 points or fewer in those matchups so the message is clear that Brooklyn has to find a way to prevent their bad stretches from snowballing.
 "Punch first. [It's as] simple as that. Punch first. If we punch first, and be aggressive, good things happen," Nets forward Julius Randle said to the media prior to the matchup against Chicago. Brooklyn has had some issues with punching first, especially against the better teams in the NBA, but the hope is that the allure of ABA Night and the lessons learned from previous losses can help this young group get off to a good start at home.
